title: Language and region
summary: One screen with two sections: the app language and the account region (ADR 0197, ADR 0298). It opens from the language row on onboarding-welcome, from chats.language and from account.region in settings-group.

language.description: The app language on this device. system follows the phone (or the browser on web): en when the first system language is English, else pt.

region.description: The id of the account's region in registries/regions.json. Before sign-up, and today for every account: br.

selectLanguage.effect: Android: sets the per-app language (LocaleManager on Android 13 and later; a stored choice that the activity applies on Android 8 to 12) and the screens change at once. iOS: opens the app's page in the system Settings (UIApplication.openSettingsURLString), where iOS keeps each app's language; iOS restarts the app after a change. Web: stores the choice in local storage and reloads the page. The next bipe-api request carries the new language in Accept-Language (ADR 0298).

selectRegion.effect: Nothing while registries/regions.json has one region: the row is checked and not a button. With two or more regions, the rules of ADR 0197 apply (an invite sets the region; a picker only without an invite).

close.effect: Back to the screen that opened it.

notes: Language section: three rows with a check mark on the current one: Igual ao celular (bipe_chats_appearance_system; web: bipe_web_appearance_system), Português (Brasil), English. The language names are in their own language on every screen. Footer bipe_settings_language_footer; on iOS bipe_settings_language_ios_footer.
Region section: one row per region of registries/regions.json, titled bipe_region_<id>, the account's region checked. Footer bipe_settings_region_footer.
The settings rows chats.language and account.region show the current value: the language name (or Igual ao celular) and the region name.
onboarding-welcome shows the current language and region as one quiet row on the cover, for example 'Português · Brasil'. It opens this screen as a sheet. The person never has to open it to sign up.
